page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.126-504 is a compute-focused flexible virtual machine instance powered by 4th generation AMD EPYC 9J14 processors based on the x86_64 architecture. The configuration supplies 126 dedicated physical cores and 252 vCPUs running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. Memory capacity totals 504.0 GB of system RAM, providing an exact 1:2 ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. No dedicated accelerators or GPUs are included.

Local physical storage is absent on this instance, necessitating network-attached block volumes for operating system disks and persistent file storage. Network connectivity features one complimentary public IPv4 address. The absence of local solid-state drives concentrates input and output throughput requirements onto remote cloud storage volumes.

With its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM configuration and high physical core density, this virtual machine functions effectively for compute-bound parallel workloads. Typical deployments include distributed batch processing, high-throughput software compilation, continuous integration pipelines, video transcoding, and scientific simulation jobs that maximize core scaling without demanding deep per-thread memory allocation.
